No frameworks. One stylesheet, one script.

Component kit

Wavefront

A complete reference of the elements a web page is likely to need, built with plain HTML, one stylesheet and one script. Flat surfaces separated by fill rather than outlines, one accent spent only on the primary action and the current state, and a change of background standing in for every hover, focus and press. The markup uses generic names, so the look can be replaced by swapping design_language.css for another language.

How the kit is put together

style

Tokens first

design_language.css

Color, type, shape, elevation, spacing and motion are all custom properties declared on :root. Components only ever read tokens, never literal values, so retheming is a single-file edit.
code

Generic names

Markup stays portable

Classes describe the role, not the language: .button-float rather than a product-specific term, .elevation-4 rather than a named shadow. The same HTML survives a change of design language.
bolt

Declarative behavior

design_language.js

Interaction is wired through data-* attributes and applied by one idempotent UI.init() pass. No inline handlers, no build step, no dependencies.

Pages

Every page is a standalone reference for one family of elements.

Using the kit

Page shell

<link rel="stylesheet" href="design_language.css">
<script src="design_language.js" defer></script>

<body class="page">
  <header class="topbar">...</header>
  <main class="page-body">
    <div class="container">...</div>
  </main>
</body>

Swapping the language

/* Any replacement stylesheet needs to define the same
   token names and the same class contract. Swapping a
   language is mostly a matter of these: how far a corner
   is cut, whether elevation is a shadow or a fill, and
   whether a label shouts. */
:root {
  --color-primary:        #2196f3;
  --color-surface:        #181a1b;
  --color-surface-sunken: #232628;
  --radius-md:            6px;
  --shadow-1:             none;
  --type-label-transform: none;
}
